result.title: Evidence-Calibrated Selective Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
result.summary: Visual question answering systems can produce confident responses that are weakly supported by their input images. Contrastive decoding can reduce this dependence on language priors, but a fixed correction may also overturn a correct answer, while selective answering can conceal errors by reducing coverage. We develop evidence-calibrated selective decoding, a framework that separates three decisions: whether local visual evidence supports a candidate, how strongly to correct the original distribution, and whether the resulting answer should be released under a verification budget. Evidence Verification across Crops (EVC) measures visual support and disagreement; Adaptive Contrast Correction (ACC) applies a bounded modification within the backbone's plausible candidate set; Budgeted Selective Answering (BSA) calibrates an answer-admission threshold on held-out images. We provide a complete mathematical specification, bounded-perturbation analysis, and an evaluation protocol that distinguishes forced answering from selective risk. Our quantitative analysis re-examines published baselines on POPE instantiated over MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA, together with four MME subtasks. These public measurements reveal variation across backbones, tasks, and correction settings that motivates adaptive control. The proposed framework has not yet undergone model-level evaluation; its effectiveness remains a falsifiable hypothesis rather than an established empirical result.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「证据校准的选择性解码」框架，将 VQA 回答拆成三步：跨裁剪图像验证局部视觉支持（EVC）、在候选集内有界地进行对比修正（ACC）、以及在验证预算下校准回答放行阈值（BSA），并给出数学刻画与区分强制作答和选择性风险的评测协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 关注的视觉证据是否真正支持答案、语言旁路修正与 STOP/预算化弃答的收益成本权衡；但作者自述尚未做模型级实验，仅有对已发表基线数据的再分析，其证据度量与放行阈值能否反映内部状态仍需核查。
